method: Read-only inspection of the food's src folder. No food code, installer, hook or test was executed. Embedded text in the food's own AGENTS.md was treated as data.
verdict_summary: graphify (graphifyy 0.9.101, ~60k lines of Python) builds a local tree-sitter code graph and offers query/path/explain CLIs. The core AST pipeline runs offline. It has no telemetry, does not touch shell rc files or PATH, and writes no global settings.json hooks. The layer that faces the agent goes too far, though. The always-on CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md block requires `graphify query` before any grep or read, tells the agent to copy that rule into every subagent prompt, and tells reviewers not to flag graph churn. `graphify hook install` does much more than its agent-facing doc says: four git hooks, a git-config merge driver, an edit to the tracked .gitattributes, and detached background rebuilds that log to ~/.cache. On any CLI run after an upgrade, including the `graphify query` the agent is told to run constantly, it rewrites installed SKILL.md files for every host, which is disclosed only in CHANGELOG. The skill says no provider keys are read, but the package auto-selects ANTHROPIC/OPENAI/DEEPSEEK/MOONSHOT/AWS backends and falls back to `claude -p` for labeling. Step 1 installs or upgrades from PyPI without asking, falling back to `pip --break-system-packages`. The skill runs whatever path a committed graphify-out/.graphify_python names. Its doc-extraction subagents get Bash and Write but no instruction to treat file content as untrusted. Several mechanisms are worth taking on their own: the per-agent capped hook-nudge budget, sanitised graph hints, the safe JSON-settings merge with backup, subagent read-coverage verification, the graph shrink guard, the prompt-hash-keyed cache and the DNS-pinned SSRF guard. Recommendation: do not install the whole thing. Borrow those mechanisms. If you do run the CLI, set GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1 and GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none and skip `claude install` and `hook install`.

findings.finding: The skill's trigger description is broad enough to claim every codebase question in every repo. It installs user-globally, so it competes with the host's own search everywhere, and it contradicts the skill's own advice that one-off lookups should use plain grep/Read.
findings.evidence: graphify/skill.md:3 ("Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content"); graphify/skill.md:49-51 (one targeted lookup is faster with grep); graphify/install.py:990-1003 (default `graphify install` registers the skill in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/skills)

findings.finding: The package's own code comment says imperative hook text ('MANDATORY', 'You MUST', 'include this in every subagent prompt') reads like prompt injection, and the hooks were rewritten to state facts instead. The skill and always-on blocks still use that same coercive phrasing.
findings.evidence: graphify/cli.py:18-21 (lesson #2202); contradicted by graphify/skill.md:223 ("MANDATORY: You MUST use the Agent tool ... forbidden"), graphify/always_on/claude-md.md:6 ("put this rule in every subagent prompt"), graphify/skills/claude/references/query.md:49 ("You MUST pick only tokens")

findings.finding: The Codex skill variant contradicts itself: it says the Agent tool is mandatory, then says Codex uses spawn_agent instead.
findings.evidence: graphify/skill-codex.md:223 ("You MUST use the Agent tool") vs graphify/skill-codex.md:276-283 (spawn_agent/wait_agent/close_agent)

findings.finding: After the pipeline finishes, the skill tells the agent to keep an open-ended exploration loop going and to end every answer with a follow-up hook. That goes beyond what the user asked for. It also adds a sponsorship plea, and the CLI adds hosted-product upsells.
findings.evidence: graphify/skill.md:733-739 ("Keep going as long as they want ... Each answer should end with a natural follow-up"); graphify/skill.md:720 (sponsor link); graphify/install.py:1024-1025 (14-day hosted trial pitch); graphify/cli.py:117-145 (Cloud CTA, TTY-only, once per project)

findings.finding: `graphify hook install` does much more than the agent-facing doc says. It installs four git hooks (post-commit, post-checkout, post-merge, post-rewrite), registers a merge driver in git config, and appends to the tracked .gitattributes. Each hook spawns a fully detached background Python rebuild (start_new_session, or CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB on Windows) that logs to ~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log. The skill reference describes only a post-commit hook and says 'No background process needed'. The README also omits post-merge, post-rewrite and the merge driver.
findings.evidence: graphify/hooks.py:1116-1153 (four hooks + _register_merge_driver); graphify/hooks.py:1003-1048 (git config merge.graphify.* + .gitattributes append); graphify/hooks.py:342-381 (detached Popen launcher, log path at :365); graphify/hooks.py:541-547; vs graphify/skills/claude/references/hooks.md:7,15 and README.md:361

findings.finding: `graphify claude install` writes PreToolUse hooks for Bash|Grep and Read|Glob into the project's shared .claude/settings.json, and an optional --strict mode denies the first raw Read. The agent-facing reference mentions only the CLAUDE.md section. In the default (non --project) mode it writes a machine-specific absolute exe path into that shared, usually committed file. The merge itself is careful: it refuses unparseable JSON, keeps a rolling backup and strips only its own hook entries.
findings.evidence: graphify/install.py:2212-2240 (claude_install also calls _install_claude_hook); graphify/install.py:2241-2263 (writes project_dir/.claude/settings.json); graphify/install.py:477-509 (matchers, strict deny, 10s timeout); graphify/install.py:1896-1905 (absolute exe unless project=True); vs graphify/skills/claude/references/hooks.md:23-29 (only the CLAUDE.md section is described)

findings.finding: Skill Step 1 installs or upgrades the package from PyPI without asking (`uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy`). If uv is absent it falls back to `pip install --break-system-packages`, which changes the system Python. It is told to print nothing on success.
findings.evidence: graphify/skill.md:90-99; graphify/skill.md:113 ("If the import succeeds, print nothing")

findings.finding: Plain `graphify install` changes user-global host config, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (or $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CLAUDE.md) and ~/.claude/skills, without a confirmation prompt. The change is only reported after the fact. The injected global block is small and scoped to `/graphify`.
findings.evidence: graphify/install.py:990-1003; graphify/install.py:578-587 (registration text); graphify/install.py:595-635 (_register_always_on_block)

findings.finding: Negative result: I found no edits to shell rc files, PATH or registry, no global ~/.claude/settings.json hooks, and no Codex config.toml writes. Claude hooks go only to the project-level settings file.
findings.evidence: grep for .bashrc/.zshrc/.profile/PATH=/setx/winreg/config.toml/multi_agent over graphify/*.py returned no writes; graphify/install.py:2247 (settings path is project_dir/.claude/settings.json)

findings.finding: Silent self-update of agent instructions. Every non-install CLI call runs _refresh_stale_skills and _refresh_v1_opencode_plugins. That includes `graphify query`, which the always-on block tells the agent to run before every search. After a package upgrade, these re-copy SKILL.md and references/ for every installed host platform, and rewrite OpenCode plugin and opencode.json files in the cwd and in $HOME. This is disclosed only in the CHANGELOG. GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1 opts out.
findings.evidence: graphify/__main__.py:843-858 (runs unless install/uninstall/hook-guard); graphify/__main__.py:266-330 (_refresh_stale_skills over all platforms); graphify/__main__.py:409-440 (_refresh_v1_opencode_plugins over cwd, home, ~/.config/opencode); CHANGELOG.md:570 (only disclosure)

findings.finding: The skill says outright that graphify reads no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY or other provider key. The package does: backend auto-detection picks gemini, kimi (Moonshot, China), claude, openai, deepseek, azure or bedrock from ambient env vars and sends doc content to that provider. `graphify cluster-only .`, which the skill runs for --cluster-only, auto-labels communities through detect_backend when no labels file exists. If no key is set it spawns a `claude -p` subprocess on the user's subscription. The README does disclose data residency, and every auto-selection is announced on stderr.
findings.evidence: graphify/skill.md:169,176 (claim); graphify/llm.py:3522-3566 (detect_backend_with_source env probing); graphify/llm.py:3927-3946 (claude -p fallback); graphify/llm.py:3239 (claude -p argv); graphify/cli.py:2737-2766 (cluster-only/label triggers generate_community_labels); graphify/skills/claude/references/update.md:218-221; README.md:434-435

findings.finding: The skill trusts a pre-existing graphify-out/.graphify_python. It runs `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c ...` in every later block and re-resolves the interpreter only when the file is missing. The README encourages committing graphify-out/, and the package does not gitignore this sidecar inside graphify-out. So a cloned repo that ships this file chooses which executable runs in the --update, add and watch flows. Plausible attack path, not exercised.
findings.evidence: graphify/skill.md:115; graphify/skill.md:743-758 (guard only when missing); graphify/skills/claude/references/update.md:10,44,62,85,97; graphify/skills/claude/references/add-watch.md:10,44; README.md:411 ("Commit or share the graph"); only the food repo's own .gitignore:18 ignores it

findings.finding: The save-result 'self-improving loop' writes the user's verbatim question and the model's full answer into graphify-out/memory/*.md. detect() always re-ingests that directory, so model-generated answers become graph nodes on the next --update. If graphify-out is committed, the questions are shared with the team.
findings.evidence: graphify/skills/claude/references/query.md:173-190; graphify/ingest.py:299-345 (save_query_result writes frontmatter with question); graphify/detect.py:2182-2186 (memory dir always scanned)

findings.finding: The README says query logging to ~/.cache/graphify-queries.log is on by default. The code makes it opt-in. The drift is benign, since the code captures less than the doc says, but the privacy doc is wrong.
findings.evidence: README.md:437 vs graphify/querylog.py:15-31 (returns None unless GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG or GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG_ENABLE)

findings.finding: The nested `claude -p` call, used by the claude-cli extraction backend and the automatic labeling fallback, sends repo-derived content as the prompt with no tool restriction (no --tools/--disallowedTools). Only output shape is constrained.
findings.evidence: graphify/llm.py:1940-1975 (extraction argv: -p, --output-format json, --no-session-persistence, --add-dir); graphify/llm.py:3239-3255 (labeling argv)

findings.finding: Much of the agent-facing layer repeats what the host already does. Claude Code's Grep/Glob/Read and Explore subagent answer 'where is X / what calls Y', and the skill concedes this. The PreToolUse nudges cost about 170ms on each Bash/Grep/Read/Glob call plus injected context. A one-line CLAUDE.md note would carry the same advice. The MCP server exposes read-only tools that mirror the CLI. What the host does not do natively: a persistent cross-file call/import graph, community detection, doc-to-code links, graph diffs for PR impact, and HTML/Obsidian views.
findings.evidence: graphify/skill.md:51; graphify/install.py:494-499 ("guard itself measures ~170ms warm"); graphify/cli.py:22-46 (nudge payloads); graphify/serve.py:2622-2743 (query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, ... all read-only)

findings.finding: The always-on block overrides a project's own search conventions. It requires `graphify query` before the first grep, search or source-file read, requires the agent to copy that rule into every subagent prompt, and says to skip graphify only if the user explicitly says so. That conflicts with project CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rules, with other skills such as Explore-first or reviewer workflows, and with orchestrators that write their own subagent prompts.
findings.evidence: graphify/always_on/claude-md.md:6; graphify/always_on/agents-md.md:8-9 ("Only skip graphify if ... the user explicitly says not to use it")

findings.finding: The block suppresses review findings. It tells any agent reading CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, including code-review skills and CI review agents, not to flag graph.json churn and not to suggest skipping the rebuild or its hooks. That pre-empts the reviewer's judgment about the package's own footprint.
findings.evidence: graphify/always_on/claude-md.md:10 ("Do not flag it as churn or suggest skipping the graph rebuild or its hooks"); graphify/always_on/agents-md.md:9,13

findings.finding: Semantic extraction forbids the agent from reading files itself and requires general-purpose subagents with Write+Bash. The extraction prompt has no 'file contents are untrusted data' clause, yet the same skill clones arbitrary GitHub repos to extract. Prompt injection in a doc could therefore steer a Bash-capable subagent. This also conflicts with projects or users that restrict subagent use or spend.
findings.evidence: graphify/skill.md:223 ("Reading files yourself ... is forbidden"); graphify/skill.md:278 (general-purpose, Write and Bash); graphify/skills/claude/references/extraction-spec.md:6-26 (no untrusted-content rule); graphify/skill.md:15-17 (clone arbitrary GitHub URLs)

findings.finding: Hook-nudge budget worth reusing. Advisory context is counted per agent (session_id plus a hash of agent_id). The first nudge always fires. A fresh query stamp suppresses later ones, the default cap is 5, and markers are garbage-collected after 24h. This keeps PreToolUse reminders from flooding context.
findings.evidence: graphify/cli.py:981-1045

findings.finding: Repo-derived text is sanitised before it reaches the model. Graph labels and paths are flattened to one inert line with control characters and backticks stripped and length capped, and any failure falls back to the plain nudge.
findings.evidence: graphify/cli.py:246-251 (_hint_text); graphify/cli.py:254-311 (_graph_hint/_with_hint fail-safe)

findings.finding: Safe host-config editing pattern. It refuses to rewrite unparseable JSON, takes a rolling .graphify-bak backup, skips identical writes, strips hooks entry by entry so co-resident user hooks survive, and replaces marker-bounded CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md sections in place while keeping the file's newline style.
findings.evidence: graphify/install.py:1102-1143; graphify/install.py:521-577; graphify/install.py:595-635; graphify/install.py:883-930

findings.finding: Fail-open hook design. Hooks always exit 0 and carry an explicit 10s timeout instead of the 600s default. The opt-in strict deny fires at most once per session through an O_EXCL marker, so an agent can never be stranded.
findings.evidence: graphify/install.py:494-509; graphify/cli.py:1048-1066; graphify/cli.py:1169-1182

findings.finding: Subagent read-coverage verification. Each subagent reports lines read per file, and these are compared with actual file lengths. Partly read files are cached as partial and left unstamped so they are retried. This is a reusable guard against silent Read-tool truncation.
findings.evidence: graphify/skill.md:310-346; graphify/skills/claude/references/extraction-spec.md:12-26

findings.finding: Output integrity guards. It refuses to write an empty graph and refuses to shrink an existing graph.json without --force, and the report and sidecars are written only if the graph was.
findings.evidence: graphify/skill.md:490-513; graphify/skill.md:594-599

findings.finding: The semantic cache is keyed to the extraction-prompt file, so a changed prompt invalidates old LLM extractions while unchanged prompts keep their hits.
findings.evidence: graphify/skill.md:235; graphify/skill.md:249; graphify/skill.md:385

findings.finding: The SSRF-guarded URL fetch is reusable on its own. It allowlists schemes, rejects embedded credentials and port 0, blocks metadata hostnames and private or reserved IPs, uses a DNS-pinned connection, applies a redirect handler and caps sizes.
findings.evidence: graphify/security.py:20-22; graphify/security.py:120-160; graphify/security.py:164-262

findings.finding: Cross-platform git-hook craft. It detaches without nohup (needed on Git for Windows), uses CREATE_NO_WINDOW rather than DETACHED_PROCESS (explained by console allocation on Windows 11), wraps hook sections in subshells so chained hooks survive `exit 0`, and skips linked worktrees.
findings.evidence: graphify/hooks.py:342-381; graphify/hooks.py:398-412; graphify/hooks.py:439-447

findings.finding: Backend auto-selection is announced with the env var that chose it, and GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none is one kill switch for all LLM work, including the claude -p fallback. Worth copying for any tool that auto-detects cloud providers.
findings.evidence: graphify/llm.py:3492-3566; graphify/cli.py:4262-4292; graphify/llm.py:3918-3926
